name: README.md
html:
diagram — the local mermaid replacement

~130KB wasm instead of ~1MB of mermaid JS. Parses, lays out, and emits SVG for the two diagram families the docs corpus uses:

FamilyCount in corpusStatus
flowchart / graph (LR/RL/TD/TB/RL, subgraphs, []/{}/()/[[]]/>] shapes, -->/-.->/---/==>, |"label"| edges, chains)22full
sequenceDiagram (participant … as, ->>/-->>/reversed arrows, self-messages, Note over)6full
everything else (mindmap, gantt, erDiagram…)0throws → caller restores source
 ```mermaid fence (docs markdown)
        │  escaped source in a .docs-mermaid div
        ▼
 experiments/docs/mermaid.ts
        │  themeJson(getComputedStyle(root)) — live CSS tokens
        ▼
 core/utils/wasm/wasm-diagram.ts        lazy, cached, unlatches on
        │  import('/wasm/diagram/…')    failure; jest-mockable seam
        ▼
 render_diagram(source, theme) → <svg>   (rust/diagram, wasm32)
        │
        ▼
 block.innerHTML = svg — real text, selectable, a11y, indexable

Why SVG and not WebGPU

Diagram text must stay real text — selectable, screen-reader reachable, indexable (the "all content readable" directive). The expensive part of mermaid was parse + layout (CPU) — wasm's sweet spot. Rasterizing a static diagram to canvas buys nothing and costs accessibility.

Layout model

  • flowchart — longest-path layering (rank(n) = 1 + max(pred)), back-edges excluded so cycles converge; barycenter ordering inside ranks (one sweep — chain-heavy graphs converge immediately); rank axis follows direction; edges clip to the target border so arrowheads land on the outline. Groups emit last-pass bounding boxes with a label strip; a final normalize pass shifts all geometry positive.
  • sequence — participants → columns in declaration order (undeclared endpoints auto-declare); one row per message; self- messages draw a stub loop; lifelines are dashed verticals; actor boxes cap the columns.

Text metrics

No DOM in wasm → widths are estimated: chars × fontSize × 0.62 (mean sans advance) + padding. If a label ever clips, raise CHAR_W in src/svg.rs — it's the single source of horizontal truth. All tuning constants are annotated at declaration with units + effects.

Theme contract

render_diagram(source, themeJson) — theme JSON is {font, fontSize, fg, bg, line, accent, surface}, mapped from live CSS custom properties by experiments/docs/mermaid.ts so diagrams follow the active palette (light/dark + accent). Every missing key falls back to a neutral value — never a hardcoded project color.

Build

cd rust/diagram
wasm-pack build --target web --release
cp pkg/luiskr_diagram* ../../website/public/wasm/diagram/

Fail-soft contract

Any parse/layout error or unsupported family throws a JsValue string — mermaid.ts catches it and restores the escaped source, so a bad diagram reads as documentation instead of breaking the page.
